bug.title: Refresh token leaks in JSON, concurrent refresh signs the user out, and the cookie only works same-site
bug.symptoms: POST /v1/auth/verify and /v1/auth/refresh still return the refresh token in the JSON body, alongside the HttpOnly cookie, so script can read it and the cookie's XSS protection is moot Two parallel POST /v1/auth/refresh with the same token -> one 200 and one 401, and the winner's new refresh token is then rejected: the race loser is treated as token theft and the whole family is revoked (identity/service.py ~331/352). Two open tabs refreshing together sign the user out The cookie is SameSite=Strict (identity/cookies.py:72), which only works when web and API share a registrable domain; nothing documents or checks that
bug.reproduction_steps: Sign in via POST /v1/auth/challenge + /verify; read refresh_token from the JSON body Fire two POST /v1/auth/refresh concurrently with the same cookie; then refresh with the winner's new cookie -> 401
bug.expected: The refresh token is delivered only as the HttpOnly cookie (Secure except on http://localhost / 127.0.0.1, Path=/v1/auth); JSON bodies carry the access token and its expiry only. A refresh token presented again within a short grace window (default 30 s, REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE_SECONDS) after it was rotated returns the same successor pair instead of revoking the family; reuse after the window still revokes the family. SameSite is configurable (REFRESH_COOKIE_SAMESITE, default Lax) and the module documents that web and API must be same-site (e.g. app.example.org and api.example.org), with a startup warning when every WEB_ORIGINS entry is cross-site from the API's own public URL
bug.actual: Token in JSON; concurrent refresh revokes the session; Strict-only cookie

constraints.constraint: Keep refresh-token rotation and family revocation on genuine reuse
Python API clients and tests that sign in over HTTP must keep working (they can read the cookie from the response)

bug.title: Web session does not survive a page load: users are signed out on every reload, full-page link and after 15 minutes
bug.symptoms: After passkey sign-in, POST /v1/auth/verify returns Set-Cookie: scholium_refresh, but the browser stores no cookie: the call is made without credentials:"include" (web-auth/signin.ts:312, lib/api/client.ts:347/576) Nothing restores the session on app load: opening /me by URL, reloading, or following any plain <a href> (moderation queue rows, dashboard "Open" links) shows "Sign in to continue" ORCID linking always fails: the return from ORCID is a full navigation to /onboarding/orcid, the in-memory token is gone, POST /v1/auth/orcid/complete -> 401 "Your session has ended" The consent page arrives signed out yet shows "Accept authorship"; clicking it posts unsigned and gets 401 with no sign-in prompt There is no way to sign out in the web app The Playwright suite treats "signed out after a page load" as expected and has no reload test
bug.reproduction_steps: Production build, web on :13000, API on :18000; sign in with a virtual passkey; reload /me -> "Sign in to continue" Onboarding: Link your ORCID iD (ORCID_MOCK) -> return page shows "Your session has ended"
bug.expected: Every auth call that sets or uses the refresh cookie (verify, refresh, logout, orcid/complete as needed) is sent with credentials:"include"; on app load a single shared bootstrap calls POST /v1/auth/refresh to restore the in-memory access token before protected pages decide the user is signed out, with concurrent callers sharing one in-flight refresh; a 401 on an authenticated call triggers one refresh-and-retry; pages that need a signed-in user redirect to /signin?next=... (consent page included) instead of offering actions that will 401; the global nav has a Sign out action (POST /v1/auth/logout, clear memory, go home); ORCID linking completes after the full-page return. New Playwright journeys in tests/e2e/session.spec.ts: sign in, reload /me and stay signed in; complete ORCID linking (mock) from onboarding; follow a moderation queue row as a moderator and stay signed in; sign out
bug.actual: Session lost on every page load; ORCID link impossible; no sign-out

constraints.constraint: The access token stays in memory only; never write tokens to localStorage/sessionStorage
All 7 existing Playwright journeys keep passing

bug.title: Legal takedowns (tombstones) cannot be issued: the record schema rejects action "tombstone"
bug.symptoms: POST /v1/moderation/decisions with action=tombstone -> 422 "tombstone is not one of [list, hold, ...]": record-core schemas/moderation.decision.json:23 lacks it, though moderation/decisions.py:147 ACTIONS has it moderation/tests/test_tombstones.py patches the schema in tests to hide this NET-5 (takedown) therefore cannot be exercised in production, though /text, /compare and /content honour the denylist
bug.reproduction_steps: As a tier-4 moderator POST a moderation.decision with action "tombstone" for a listed version's PDF cid -> 422
bug.expected: The shared schema allows "tombstone" (with whatever required fields decisions.py expects, e.g. a legal basis/reason), the API accepts it from tier 4 only, the test fixture that patches the schema is removed, and the web verify-core accepts tombstone decisions when verifying a paper's records

constraints.constraint: Python and TS cores must keep agreeing on the shared vectors

bug.title: Authors and moderators see 404 for unlisted papers' checks, text and PDF; moderation detail shows no paper
bug.symptoms: The web fetches checks, text and content without a token (submit/checks.ts:110-113 auth:false "public, no token"), while the API now serves unlisted checks/text/content only to authors and moderators: the author's status tracker and step 4 show nothing; the author's own unlisted paper page has no text /mod/{cid} shows only metadata and the decision form, no PDF and no text; design.md section 5.7 requires "Detail view shows the paper beside a decision form" The decision form does not offer the tombstone (legal takedown) action
bug.reproduction_steps: As an author, submit a version and open the status tracker: GET .../checks -> 404 (200 with the author's token) As a moderator open /mod/{cid} for a queued version: 0 canvases, no text
bug.expected: Checks, text and content requests send the bearer token when signed in (still working anonymously for listed papers); the moderation detail view renders the version's PDF (existing PDF viewer) and extracted text beside the decision form per design.md, and the decision form offers tombstone with a required legal reason, visible only to tier 4

bug.title: Upload size and storage are effectively unlimited for new accounts
bug.symptoms: A new tier-2 account can declare a 5 GiB upload (201) Completed uploads have no per-DID storage quota and are never cleaned up if no manifest ever references them; /uploads is exempt from the write limit
bug.reproduction_steps: As a new tier-2 account POST /v1/uploads with Upload-Length 5 GiB -> 201; complete many 50 MB uploads that are never referenced
bug.expected: Per-DID quotas: bytes in flight and bytes completed-but-unreferenced per day (configurable, defaults sized for Phase 1: e.g. 2 GiB/day for accounts under 90 days, 20 GiB/day otherwise), 413/429 problem when exceeded; a periodic job deletes completed uploads not referenced by any manifest after UPLOAD_ORPHAN_TTL (default 7 days); the 5 GiB bundle cap stays for accounts that are allowed it
bug.actual: No quota; orphaned files kept forever

bug.title: Co-authors who never consented, or declined, can retract or withdraw a paper
bug.symptoms: submissions/notices.py ~360-391 paper_authors counts every author listed on a version, not only those whose coauthor.consent accepted it
bug.reproduction_steps: List an author on v1 who never consents (or declines); have them sign a retraction notice -> accepted
bug.expected: Only authors with an accepted consent on a listed version of the paper (or tier-4 moderators) may issue withdrawal, retraction, correction or response notices; others get 403 problem

bug.title: Every content download scans all manifests in the log
bug.symptoms: content/visibility.py ~74-79 resolves which versions reference a cid by scanning every manifest record on each GET /v1/content/{cid}; cost grows with the node
bug.reproduction_steps: Seed many papers; time GET /v1/content/{cid}: proportional to the number of manifests
bug.expected: A content-reference index (content cid -> version cid) maintained by a ledger subscriber and backfilled on startup makes the visibility check an indexed lookup; behaviour (who may read what) is unchanged

bug.title: Production refusal is bypassed by SCHOLIUM_ENV spelling and accepts several unsafe values
bug.symptoms: validate_for_environment checks SCHOLIUM_ENV == "production" exactly; "Production" or "prod" with every dev default starts the app With production set it still accepts an empty node key file, COMMITTEE_PUBLIC_KEY="x" (not a key), RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=0 and http:// WEB_ORIGINS
bug.reproduction_steps: SCHOLIUM_ENV=prod with dev defaults -> app starts
bug.expected: SCHOLIUM_ENV is normalised (case-insensitive; prod/production mean production; unknown values refuse to start); production additionally refuses an empty or unparsable node key file, a COMMITTEE_PUBLIC_KEY that does not parse as the expected key type, RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=0, and non-https WEB_ORIGINS

bug.title: Every paper view downloads the whole public log to verify one paper
bug.symptoms: paper-proof/source.ts ~60-66,114 pages through GET /v1/sync/range from 0 (up to MAX_SYNC_PAGES=100 x 500) on each Proof tab view; past 50k log entries the browser proof refuses ("log is too long")
bug.reproduction_steps: Open any paper's Proof tab and watch the network: sync/range pages from 0
bug.expected: The Proof tab fetches only the paper's records with their signatures and log proofs (a per-paper endpoint such as GET /v1/papers/{id}/records, or the existing per-paper CAR export) and verifies them client-side with verify-core; the verdict is the same as before and as `scholium verify --node`

bug.title: Authors have no UI for a new version, notices or appeals (PUB-6, PUB-7, MOD-2)
bug.symptoms: The paper page never links to the existing new-version form (submit/new-version-link.tsx is not mounted) There is no UI to issue a correction, retraction or withdrawal notice; the API supports them There is no UI to file an appeal against a moderation decision on one's paper; POST /v1/appeals works
bug.reproduction_steps: Sign in as the consented author of a listed paper and open /p/{id}: no New version, notice or appeal actions
bug.expected: For consented authors of the paper the header actions offer: New version (to the existing form), Issue notice (correction/retraction/withdrawal; signed with the web signer; confirmation for retraction/withdrawal) and, when the latest moderation decision on the paper is a hold/reject, File an appeal (reason, signed, POST /v1/appeals). Per design.md; hidden for everyone else

bug.title: No UI to endorse a researcher (ID-5)
bug.symptoms: The endorsement API works (tier 2 in a category may endorse), but no page lets a user endorse another
bug.reproduction_steps: As a tier-2 user endorsed in cs.AI, open /u/{did} of a tier-1 user: no Endorse action
bug.expected: The public profile shows Endorse in {category} for each category the signed-in viewer may endorse in (from the API's rules), signs and posts the endorsement record, and reflects the new tier; hidden otherwise

bug.title: Reviewers cannot update a review against a new version in the UI (REV-5)
bug.symptoms: The API accepts review updates (a review.formal whose prev is the reviewer's earlier one) but no UI offers it; the reviews tab shows no Update action when a newer version exists
bug.reproduction_steps: Reveal a review on v1; the author posts v2; as the reviewer open the reviews tab: no way to revise against v2
bug.expected: When the signed-in reviewer's revealed review targets an older version than the paper's latest, the reviews tab shows Update for v{latest}, opening the review form prefilled with the current rubric; submitting signs and posts the update with prev set; the history shows both

bug.title: Browser journeys do not cover moderation, review, endorsement and author actions
bug.symptoms: The Playwright suite covers reading, discussion, submit and /me only
bug.reproduction_steps: npm run test:e2e lists 7 journeys (plus the session journeys added by the session fix)
bug.expected: Additional real-browser journeys in tests/e2e/roles.spec.ts pass: a moderator opens the queue, sees the paper's PDF and text beside the decision form and lists it; two reviewers commit, one reveals, then after the second reveals the reports show; the author posts a new version and the reviewer updates; a tier-2 user endorses a newcomer and their tier changes; an author issues a correction notice and the banner appears; an author files an appeal on a held paper

constraints.constraint: Seed via the existing seed-demo/admin CLI; no test-only API routes
